questions.question: A circle is inscribed in a quadrilateral ABCD, touching sides AB, BC, CD and DA at P, Q, R and S, respectively. If AS = 8 cm, BC = 11 cm, and CR = 5 cm, then the length AB is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AS = 8 cm, BC = 11 cm and CR = 5 cm,

**Concept used:**

If from one external point, two tangents are drawn to a circle then they have equal tangent segments.

**Formula used:**

AB + CD = AD + BC

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6319a407052bca3b0d02c71df737ed66e1462cf3f96e045452ff1115a48335bf.png] **

⇒ CR = CQ = 5 cm

⇒ BQ = BC - CQ = 11 - 5 = 6 cm

⇒ BQ = BP = 6 cm ----(1)

⇒ AS = AP = 8 cm ----(2)

Therefore,

AB = AP + BP = 8 + 6 = 14

questions.question:
The radius of the base of a cylinder is 7 cm and its curved surface area is 4400 cm². Its volume (in Cm³) will be: 

Take π = 22/7
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of cylinder = 7cm

Curved surface area = 4400cm²

**Formula used:**

Curved surface area of the cylinder = 2πrh

The volume of cylinder = πr²h

where r → radius 

h → height of the cylinder

**Calculation:**

Curved surface area = 2πrh

⇒ 2πrh = 4400

⇒ πrh = 2200

Volume = πr²h

⇒ πrh × r = 2200 × 7 = 15400 cm³

questions.question: If 3 - 2sin²θ - 3cosθ = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then find the value of (2cosecθ + tanθ)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

3 - 2sin²θ - 3cosθ = 0

**Formula: **

sin2θ + cos²θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ 3 - 2(1 - cos2θ) - 3cosθ = 0

⇒ 3 - 2 + 2cos2θ - 3cosθ = 0

⇒ 2cos2θ - 3cosθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2cos2θ - 2cosθ - cosθ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2cosθ(cosθ - 1 ) - 1(cosθ - 1) = 0

⇒ (2cosθ - 1)(cosθ - 1 ) = 0

⇒ cosθ = (1/2), cosθ = 1

⇒ cosθ = (1/2)

⇒ cosθ = cos60°

⇒ θ = 60°

Now, (2cosecθ + tanθ)

⇒ 2cosec60° + tan60°

⇒ {2 × (2/√3)} + √3

⇒ (4/√3) + √3

⇒ (4 + 3)/√3

⇒ 7/√3

⇒ 7√3/3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Since, 0° 

3 - 2sin245 - 3cos45 = 3 - 2 × 1/2 - 3 × 1/√2 = (2√2 - 3)/√2 ≠ 0

Again, take θ = 60, then

3 - 2sin260 - 3cos60 = 3 - 2 × 3/4 - 3/2 = 3 - 3 = 0 satisfied

Now, (2cosecθ + tanθ) = 2cosec60° + tan60° 

⇒ {2 × (2/√3)} + √3

⇒ 7/√3 = 7√3/3

questions.question: If a + b + c = 5, and a² + b² + c² = 33, then find the value of a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc
questions.solution:
**Given:**

a + b + c = 5

(a + b + c)² = 25

**Formula used:**

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 - ab - bc - ca)

**Calculation:**

⇒ a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca) = 25

⇒ 2(ab + bc + ca) = 25 - 33 = -8

⇒ (ab + bc + ca) = (-8)/2 = -4

a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² - ab - bc - ca)

⇒ 5 × {33 - (-4)} = 5 × 37 = 18

questions.question: The total number of students in class A and B is 96. The number of students in A is 40% more than that in B. The average weight (in kg) of the students in B is 50% more than that of the students in A. If the average weight of all the students in A and B taken together is 58 kg, then what is the average weight of the students in B?
questions.solution:
Let the number of students in class B be x.

The total number of students in class A and B = 96

The number of students in class A = the number of students in class B × 140/100

⇒ 1.4x + x = 96

⇒ x = 96/2.4 = 40

The number of students in class A = 40 × 140/100 = 56

Let the average weight of students in class A be y.

⇒ The average weight of students in class B = y × 150/100 = 1.5y

Total average weight of all the students in A and B taken together = 58

According to the question,

y × 56 + 1.5y × 40 = 58 × 96

⇒ y = 48

The average weight (in kg) of the students in B = 1.5y = 1.5 × 48

= 72

questions.question: A and B, working together, can be complete a work in 16 days, C and A together can complete in 32 days, B and C together can complete it in 24 days. They worked together for 12 days. In how many days will C alone complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A + B can complete a work = 16 days

C + A can complete a work = 32 days 

B + C can complete a work = 24 days

**Concept used:**

Total work = Efficiency × Time 

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be 96.

(Lcm of 16, 32 and 24 is 96)

Efficiency of (A + B) = 6

Efficiency of (B + C) = 4

Efficiency of (C + A) = 3

Efficiency of 2(A + B + C) = 13

Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 6.5

Work of 12 days = 6.5 × 12 = 78

Remaining work = 96 - 78 = 18

Efficiency of C = 6.5 - 6 = 0.5

Days to complete remaining work = 18/0.5 = 36 days

questions.question: Anu spends 90% of her income. If her expenditure increase by 25% and saving increase by 30%, then by what percent does her salary increase?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Anu's spending = 90% of income

Increase in expenditure = 25%

Increase in saving = 30%

**Formula used:**

Income = Expenditure + Saving

**Calculation:**

Let the total income of Anu = 100

Expenditure = 90 × 100/100 = 90

Saving = 100 - 90 = 10

Now, Expenditure = 90 × 125/100 = 112.5

Saving = 10 × 130/100 = 13

⇒ 112.5 + 13 = 125.50

Required percentage = 25.5 × 100/100 = 25.5%

questions.question: What is the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 4, 096 at 15% p.a. for 2(1)/(2) years, if the interest is compound 10 - monthly?

Effective rate of interest 

12 months = 15%

10 months = 12.5%

Effective rate of interest = 12.5% (compounded 10 monthly)

Now, 

When calculated at compound interest

Amount (A) = p(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Where p, r and n are principal, rate and time respectively

A = 4096(1 + 12.5/100)³

Compound Interest = Amount – Principal

 Compound Interest = 5832 – 4096 = 1736

questions.question: Abhi sold two articles for Rs. 5, 220 each. On one, he gained 16% and on the other, he lost 10%. His profit or loss on the whole transaction was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

S.P. of two articles = Rs. 5220 each

Gain% on 1st article = 16%

Loss% on 2nd article = 10%

**Formula used:**

C.P. of an article = (S.P. × 100)/(100 + gain%)

**Calculation:**

Selling price of two articles = 5220 × 2 = 10440

Cost price of 1st article = 5220 × 100/116 = 4500

Cost price of 2ⁿd article = 5220 × 100/90 = 5800

Cost price of two articles = 4500 + 5800 = 10300

Profit = 10440 - 10300 = Rs. 140

questions.question: Train x running at 84 km/h crosses another train y running at 52 km/h in opposite direction in 12 seconds. If the length of train y is two-third that of x then find the length of train x.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of train x = L₁

Length of train y = L₂

Speed of train x = 84 km/h

Speed of train y = 52 km/h

**Formula used:**

If two objects are running in the same direction, then

Relative speed = S₁ - S₂

If two objects are running in the opposite direction, then 

Relative speed = S1 + S2

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 84 + 52 = 136 × 5/18 m/s

Length of train x and y = time × relative speed

Length of train x and y = 12 × 136 × 5/18 = 1360/3

⇒ L₁ + L₂ = 1360/3

⇒ L₁ + {L₁ × (2/3)} = 1360/3

⇒ 5/3 L₁ = 1360/3

⇒ L₁ = 272 m
